item.title: RT: My colleagues @LizAnnSonders and @KevRGordon call it a “duck market.” For much o
item.description:
My colleagues @LizAnnSonders and @KevRGordon call it a “duck market.” For much of this year, the S&P 500 looked fairly calm even as stocks were paddling hard underneath.

Lately, you can see the chop from shore. The S&P 500 ended last week 11.6% below its record. Tech led Monday’s rally and then pulled the S&P 500 lower this morning.

There’s more in this chart than I usually show, but start with energy and airlines. When oil prices surged in the spring, energy stocks led and airlines struggled. As oil eased in November, they traded places.

Then look at chips. Even after Monday’s 15% jump, semiconductor stocks still trailed the S&P 500 by nearly 8 percentage points over the past month. That’s what gives me pause when I hear a confident prediction about the winners from AI. I believe that AI will change how businesses operate but I’m less confident about which stocks will lead along the way. That’s one reason we favor broad equity exposure.
